review.open_twice: "Probably yes on substance. The Gotchas section (lines 268-301) is genuinely strong and concrete -- the visibility/reconstruction distinction, post-synthesis name mapping, restore-hides-the-precondition, wrapped-buffer-as-finding are all real, non-generic transferred experience -- and the skill is unusually disciplined about not inventing vendor-specific facts. But the retrieval-budget section is the one place this pack asks an engineer to trust a mechanical accounting claim ('make sure NO step exceeds it'), and on a close read that claim is visibly false (step 5 opens files the budget says it doesn't). A careful reader who checks that arithmetic once and finds it wrong is likely to start distrusting the rest of the document's precision, which is a real cost for a skill whose whole value proposition is precision under a hard budget."

recheck.why: Lint is 1.000 and clean, role/level are exactly emulation-engineer/staff, all nine slots are spent, the Grep/Read itemisation adds up (1 Glob; 2+1+4+1 = 8 Grep; 2+1+1 = 4 Read), and every handoff field has an assigning step and agrees with _shared/handoff-vocabulary.md (`phase` and `class` full canonical sets; `window` free text, explicitly blessed by the vocabulary's own note; `signature`/`run id`/`owner`/`notes` per the shape rules, `notes` last; `visibility`, `locus`, `probes`, `restore`, `recompile`, `trigger`, `arm fallback` are unique to this skill in the pack; `coverage` and `export` are free text everywhere they appear). But the skill gets the buffer-wrap diagnosis backwards, and it is backwards in a way that fires on the configuration the skill itself recommends. Step 2 line 161: "what the capture report says about the buffer — filled, wrapped, or partly used. A wrapped buffer means the earliest samples are gone, and the window was on the wrong side of the trigger", echoed in the Gotchas at line 378: "A wrapped buffer is a finding, not a failure. It says the trigger fired later than the window needed, which tells you the split from step 4 was backwards." That is wrong. A trace buffer serving a pre-trigger window is circular and must be sampling continuously before the trigger arrives; on any emulation run longer than the buffer depth — i.e. essentially all of them — it wraps many times by construction and that is the success case. Step 4 line 221 explicitly tells the reader "A trigger on the failure itself needs an almost entirely pre-trigger window", so the skill's own recommended setup reports as wrapped on a healthy capture, and its own step-2 rule then tells the engineer the window was on the wrong side of the trigger. That sends them to re-plan a correct window and burn a four-hour round. The real check — which the skill never asks for anywhere — is whether the captured cycle range contains the locus from step 2. The skill actually knows this: line 405 names the true failure mode correctly ("sets an all-post-trigger window on a trigger that fires at the failure"), but reaches it through a buffer-state word instead of a range comparison. Compounding it, "filled, wrapped, or partly used" are three capture-report states the author invented; the skill was careful enough to add slots for the arm/fire strings and the failed/clean strings but gave the capture report's own buffer vocabulary no slot at all, and a whole diagnosis plus a feedback edge into step 4 rests on it. Second, smaller: step 2 line 154 anchors a Read on something no Grep looked for — "one in the capture report at the buffer line the second Grep found" — but the second Grep searched the report for the arm and fire strings from the Trigger mechanism slot, not for a buffer line. The stated fallback ("or at its head if that call returned no hit there") only covers the case where there is no arm/fire hit at all, so the ordinary case (arm/fire hit present, no buffer line among the hits) falls through both branches with no anchor. I would not hand this to a working DV engineer today: the one step every later step branches off contains a rule that misdiagnoses a correct capture.
remaining: Step 2 (line 161) and Gotcha (line 378): the wrapped-buffer inference is wrong. A circular trace buffer serving the almost-entirely-pre-trigger window that step 4 line 221 recommends wraps continuously by design; wrapping is the normal state of a successful pre-trigger capture, not evidence that 'the window was on the wrong side of the trigger' or that 'the split from step 4 was backwards'. Wrapping only tells you the capture ran longer than the buffer depth.

The check that would actually diagnose a backwards split is missing from the procedure and from the Human-verification list: compare the captured cycle range against the locus from step 2 and say whether the locus is inside it. Line 405 already names the failure mode correctly ('sets an all-post-trigger window on a trigger that fires at the failure') but no step derives it.

'filled, wrapped, or partly used' is capture-report vocabulary the author could not know and no slot declares. The skill has slots for the arm/fire strings (Trigger mechanism) and the failed/clean strings (Run log and markers) but none for what the capture report calls buffer states — yet step 2's fourth recorded item, the Gotcha at line 378, and the feedback edge into step 4 all depend on it.

Step 2 line 154: 'one in the capture report at the buffer line the second Grep found' — the second Grep searched for arm and fire strings, not for a buffer line, so there is no such hit to anchor on. The 'or at its head' fallback is scoped only to 'if that call returned no hit there', leaving the common case (arm/fire hit found, no buffer line) with no anchor at all.

Step 6 line 262: on full-replay, 'leave the rest of the budget for step 7's cadence' promises a reallocation the itemisation at lines 93-103 does not offer — step 7 is capped at one Grep and shares the single spare Read. Saved calls are simply unspent, not transferable. Minor, and safe (under-spend), but the prose overclaims.

Steps 6 (line 279) and 7 (line 287) both claim 'the spare Read window' and the text acknowledges the contention ('step 7 is the only other claim on it') without ever giving a tie-break. The stopping rule absorbs it, but which step wins is left to the reader.
